findings: Acceptance addressed by tests and independent source review: both legacy-v0 and split-v1 stores preserve original source bytes, project revisions/facts/handoffs and artifacts; committed WAL is backed up. Unchanged migrations repeat without writes, changed sources/destinations refuse overwrite, and restore-copy recovers pre-migration data into new roots after live-store changes. Shared transaction rollback and orphan rejection are exercised. Historical evaluations are quarantined and accepted runs remain immutable; fresh Gate execution is required. Unknown contract properties, unsupported schema versions, malformed/incomplete manifests and aliased nested roots are refused. The four JSON schemas exactly match runtime models. These checks use a fake executor for authority regressions and do not establish real execution isolation or release authority. Independent review report is required separately at completion; operational recovery limits remain disclosed.
risks: Offline migration requires all source writers to be stopped; local writable manifests and SQLite are not a hostile-writer security boundary.
A killed migration may leave a publication lock and private staging; no automatic stale-lock recovery.
Interrupted Gate attach preserves partial files and refuses retries until inspected; automatic recovery is not implemented.
Windows loopback isolation remains unresolved; measure-only is REVIEW and no release is authorized.
UnitExecutor is a test double, not evidence of a real isolated runtime. No cost savings or advanced-project success were measured.
